slots.practicalActivity: Implement gradient boosting from scratch by fitting a short sequence of shallow DecisionTreeRegressors to the residuals of the previous ensemble on a synthetic churn table. Then split the same data into fit/validation/test sets, train an XGBClassifier with early_stopping_rounds=30 watching validation AUC, and compare its test AUC against both your from-scratch version and a logistic regression baseline.
slots.deliverable: A printed 3-way test AUC comparison (from-scratch boosting, XGBClassifier with early stopping, logistic regression baseline) plus a note on which boosting round XGBoost's early stopping selected as best.

slots.practicalActivity: Train LGBMClassifier and CatBoostClassifier on the same churn dataset used for XGBoost, comparing training speed and test AUC against the XGBoost result from the previous slot. Then tune the strongest of the three with RandomizedSearchCV over learning_rate, max_depth/num_leaves, and subsample/colsample parameters.
slots.deliverable: A 3-library comparison table (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) with test AUC and training time, plus the tuned winner's best_params_ and its improved test AUC.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same dataset, fit a RandomForestClassifier and your best boosted model side by side under identical cross-validation. Compare test AUC, training time, and sensitivity to a handful of deliberately mislabeled rows you inject, then write 3 sentences on when you would pick each one in a real project.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side boosting-vs-random-forest comparison table (AUC, training time, noise sensitivity) with a written 3-sentence recommendation for when to use each.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Boosting: on one tabular dataset of your choosing, run a full boosting bake-off - plain gradient boosting, XGBoost with early stopping, LightGBM, CatBoost, and a random forest baseline - all under the same cross-validation, and declare a winner using only test-set evidence.
slots.deliverable: A single comparison report ranking all 5 models by test-set AUC or accuracy, with a one-paragraph justification for the declared winner.

slots.practicalActivity: Decompose a real or synthetic weekly time series into trend, seasonality, and residual with statsmodels' seasonal_decompose. Then run an Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for stationarity and plot the ACF/PACF of both the raw series and its first difference to see which one looks stationary.
slots.deliverable: A decomposition plot (trend/seasonal/residual) plus an ADF test result and ACF/PACF plots for the raw and differenced series, with a written stationarity conclusion.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a naive forecast (last value repeated) and a seasonal naive forecast (same value from one season ago) for your time series, holding out the last several periods as a test window, and compute MAE for each to establish the baseline every later model in this chapter must beat.
slots.deliverable: A baseline comparison table (naive vs. seasonal naive MAE) on a held-out test window, to be used as the benchmark for every later forecasting lesson.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit Holt-Winters exponential smoothing (statsmodels ExponentialSmoothing) and an ARIMA or SARIMA model on the same series and held-out window, comparing their MAE against the naive baseline from the previous slot.
slots.deliverable: A 3-row MAE comparison table (naive baseline, exponential smoothing, ARIMA/SARIMA) on the same held-out test window.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit a default Prophet model on a series spanning under 2 years and print m.seasonalities to confirm yearly seasonality was silently left off. Then refit with yearly_seasonality=True and compare the MAE before and after that one-argument fix, reproducing the exact gotcha the lesson demonstrates.
slots.deliverable: A before/after MAE comparison (default Prophet vs. yearly_seasonality=True) with the printed m.seasonalities list proving the fix, plus a saved plot_components() chart.

slots.practicalActivity: Build lag and calendar features (lagged values, day-of-week, week-of-year sine/cosine) for your series and train a GradientBoostingRegressor or RandomForestRegressor forecaster. Run a proper rolling-origin backtest (not a single train/test split) comparing it against the naive, exponential smoothing, and Prophet results from earlier slots using the same MAE measure.
slots.deliverable: A rolling-origin backtest table comparing at least 4 forecasting approaches (naive, statistical, Prophet, machine learning) with MAE averaged across multiple backtest windows.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Time-Series Forecasting: pick one real or synthetic business time series and run the full forecasting bake-off from this chapter (naive, exponential smoothing/ARIMA, Prophet, machine learning with lag features) through a single rolling-origin backtest harness, reporting a ranked final table.
slots.deliverable: One consolidated rolling-origin backtest report ranking at least 4 forecasting methods by MAE, with a plotted forecast-vs-actual chart for the winning method.

slots.practicalActivity: Clean and tokenize a small set of real text documents (e.g. product reviews or headlines you collect, or a public text dataset), then build both a CountVectorizer bag-of-words matrix and a TfidfVectorizer matrix on the same corpus, fitting only on a training split. Use cosine_similarity to find the most similar document to a new query sentence you write.
slots.deliverable: A fitted CountVectorizer and TfidfVectorizer (fit on training text only) plus a cosine-similarity query result showing the single most similar document to an original test sentence.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the TF-IDF features from the previous slot (or sklearn's fetch_20newsgroups restricted to 2-3 categories), train a classifier (LogisticRegression or MultinomialNB) to predict document category, and report precision, recall, and F1 per class on a held-out test split.
slots.deliverable: A trained text classifier plus a per-class precision/recall/F1 classification report on real held-out documents.

slots.practicalActivity: Train a positive/negative sentiment classifier on a labeled review dataset using TF-IDF features and logistic regression, then run it on 5 original sentences you write yourself and check whether its predictions match your own judgment.
slots.deliverable: A trained sentiment classifier with its test accuracy, plus predictions and your own agreement check on 5 original sentences.

slots.practicalActivity: Run Latent Dirichlet Allocation (sklearn's LatentDirichletAllocation) on a real text corpus with 5-8 topics, print the top 10 words for each topic, and manually assign each discovered topic a short, human-readable label based on its top words.
slots.deliverable: A fitted topic model with the top-10-words list per topic and a written human-assigned label for each topic.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a small user-item interaction matrix (e.g. 60 users by 30 items, binary clicked/not-clicked, generated the way the course's illustrative click matrix is) and compute a simple popularity-based recommendation list (most-clicked items overall) as the baseline every personalized method must beat.
slots.deliverable: A user-item interaction matrix plus a popularity-baseline top-5 recommendation list, to be compared against the personalized methods in the next 2 lessons.

slots.practicalActivity: On that same interaction matrix, implement item-based and user-based collaborative filtering with cosine_similarity, and matrix factorization with TruncatedSVD. Compare the top-5 recommendations each of the 3 methods produces for 2 specific users against the popularity baseline from the previous slot.
slots.deliverable: A 3-method recommendation comparison (item-based, user-based, SVD) for 2 real users, each compared against the popularity baseline.

slots.practicalActivity: Build item feature vectors (e.g. TF-IDF on item descriptions, or one-hot category encodings) and recommend items similar to a given item purely by content similarity. Then recommend for a brand-new item that has zero interactions, to show content-based recommendation solves collaborative filtering's cold-start problem.
slots.deliverable: A content-based similarity recommendation list for an existing item and for a brand-new, zero-interaction item, demonstrating the cold-start fix.

slots.practicalActivity: Split your interaction data into train/test by holding out some of each user's real clicks, then compute precision@k and recall@k for the collaborative-filtering and content-based recommenders from the last two slots, and declare which one ranks held-out clicks better.
slots.deliverable: A precision@k/recall@k comparison table for at least 2 recommender approaches, evaluated on real held-out interactions.

slots.practicalActivity: Take a trained gradient-boosted or random-forest classifier from earlier in this course, compute its built-in feature_importances_ and compare them against sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance on the same held-out test data. Note any feature that ranks very differently between the two methods and write one sentence on why that can happen.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side feature-importance table (built-in vs. permutation importance) for one real trained model, with a written note explaining any disagreement between the two rankings.

slots.practicalActivity: Run shap.TreeExplainer on your trained gradient-boosted model, print the global mean-absolute-SHAP ranking, and generate a beeswarm summary_plot. Then pick one individual row, produce a waterfall plot, and confirm the base value plus that row's contributions sum exactly to the model's real output for that row.
slots.deliverable: A SHAP beeswarm summary plot, a single-row waterfall plot, and a printed base-value-plus-contributions check that matches the model's actual output for that row.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a 1-page plain-language explanation of your SHAP results for a non-technical stakeholder. Then check your model's predictions for a fairness gap across a sensitive grouping column (e.g. comparing false-positive and false-negative rates between 2 groups in your data) and report whether a meaningful disparity exists.
slots.deliverable: A stakeholder-facing explanation memo plus a fairness audit table comparing error rates across at least 2 groups in the real data.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Model Explainability: pick one model from earlier in the course and build a complete explainability package for it - permutation importance, a SHAP summary and waterfall plot, and a fairness check across one grouping column - packaged as a single explainability report.
slots.deliverable: One consolidated explainability report combining permutation importance, SHAP plots, and a fairness audit for a single real trained model.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: Forecast and Explain a Business Outcome

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a real or realistic time-series business outcome to forecast and explain (e.g. weekly demand, signups, or revenue). Write the framing sentence naming the forecast horizon and the business decision it feeds, seal off the final weeks as an untouched test window, and compute the naive/seasonal-naive baseline MAE on a backtest as the number every later model must beat.
slots.deliverable: A written capstone framing document naming the forecast horizon and decision, a sealed final-weeks test file, and a baseline backtest MAE to beat.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a regression-on-log-demand forecast (modeling calendar, trend, and promotion features with OLS or similar) and a detrend-plus-gradient-boosting forecast. Compare both against the sealed capstone's naive baseline using a rolling-origin backtest, then explain the strongest driver (e.g. a promotion or seasonal effect) with both regression coefficients and SHAP values, confirming the two explanations agree.
slots.deliverable: A rolling-origin backtest table ranking the naive baseline against a regression model and a machine-learning model, plus a driver explanation backed by both regression coefficients and SHAP that agree on the same top driver.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the capstone's sealed final test window exactly once, compute the real final forecast error (MAE) for your winning model, then write a 1-page portfolio presentation covering the business framing, the backtest comparison, the explained driver, and the one-time final test result.
slots.deliverable: A portfolio-ready capstone write-up containing the one-time sealed-test-set MAE, the winning model's explained top driver, and a summary ready for a GitHub portfolio repository.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can train and tune gradient-boosted models (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost), build and honestly backtest a time-series forecast, classify and explore real text with NLP techniques, build and evaluate a recommender system, and explain any model's predictions with permutation importance and SHAP - closing with a forecasting capstone whose results are backed by two independent explanation methods that agree.
